messages:
alex: quick idea — what if we add a lightweight 'guardrail' tag on saved queries that enforces routing/quota hints during rollouts?
alex: e.g. a saved query could carry metadata like `policy_tag: cost_guarded` that the routing layer reads to prefer cheaper model variants and respect hard token caps.
ryan: +1 for making it explicit. we need to be careful about UX though — folks expect saved queries to be just filters, not policy. how do we show this in the console?
maria: maybe a small badge on the query chip: "Guardrail: cost" with tooltip -> shows enforced routing policy and preview burn estimate. keeps the main name clean. :mag_right:
ryan: preview burn estimate is big — we can compute an expected token burn for the route/model combo, show a range. but that needs telemetry sampling to be accurate.
sophie: telemetry note: our sampling rate is uneven across routes. if UI shows an estimate, add a little disclaimer and a link to 'sampling health' for that route. otherwise support will get flooded.
alex: agree. UX idea: two-line chip: title on the left, small meta icons on the right (guardrail badge, sampling icon, preview-cost). click expands to details panel.
maria: expansion panel should include a minimal API preview for infra folks, like: ```json
{
  "saved_query_id": "sq_123",
  "policy_tag": "cost_guarded",
  "routing_hint": "prefer:tiny-quant",
  "token_estimate": "~120-250"
}
```
maria: exposing that helps integrators who call the Management API.
ryan: ok, but we have to think about backward compatibility for Management API: if saved_query gains `policy_tag`, older SDKs should ignore it. plan: add as optional metadata field and include a migration note in the API changelog.
sophie: rollout guardrails also need a fallback mode — if the preferred cheap variant is unavailable, should we: 1) fallback to more expensive model, 2) block request, or 3) queue to dedicated pool? we need a per-tag default.
alex: propose `policy_tag` -> config object with `on_unavailable: [fallback, block, queue]`. default = fallback to the next cheapest. teams can choose block for strict cost control.
ryan: for quota enforcement, saved_query should optionally carry a `hard_token_limit` that console honors and shows red when preview > limit. audience: platform customers who want predictable burn per-run.
maria: UX microcopy: when someone clicks save with a hard limit, show a modal: "This saved query will enforce a per-request token cap at the routing layer. Calls that exceed it may be blocked." confirm checkbox.
sophie: telemetry: add events `saved_query.guardrail.applied` and `saved_query.guardrail.blocked` with route, model_variant, sampling_rate. we can then monitor false positives and tune heuristics.
ryan: question for infra: is the runtime able to read saved-query metadata on the wire cheaply, or do we need a caching sync job?
alex: runtime can read tags from request headers if the Console embeds them in the call. alternative: attach `sq_metadata_id` to the route and runtime fetches from config store — requires versioned config. both doable, tradeoffs on latency.
sophie: small thought — for ephemeral previews (preview tab in Console) we should ignore `block` mode and just show a simulated enforcement result. no one expects preview to actually block.
maria: +1. previews should never mutate routing state. show simulation badge and a link: "View expected enforcement (simulated)".
ryan: final ask: add a small API contract doc for this new field and a migration plan in the next release notes. I'll draft it and ping @maria for wording.
alex: thanks. @deploy-bot any objection to adding feature flag `sq_guardrails_v1` for initial rollout?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag created: `sq_guardrails_v1` (off by default). Use with `--ff` on Console canary. :white_check_mark:
maria: awesome — I'll put sketches into the console Figma, include badge visuals and the confirm modal.
sophie: can we add a telemetry gate so we only enable preview-cost computations for 10% of heavy routes at first? avoids spikes.
ryan: yep, add sampling gate on compute job. i'll add it to the infra tickets.
alex: ok team, next steps: Maria UI mocks + microcopy, Ryan infra API + migration note, Sophie telemetry events + sampling gate. will sync tomorrow at 11. :calendar: 
maria: noted.
